column1: # THE CARRIERS THE GOOSE HOSTILE-CORPUS RUNNER DOES NOT READ
# carrier: its manifest name, a tab, and one line saying why. Every case of a
# carrier named here is counted as held; a carrier the runner answers absent
# that no line names fails the ledger, and so does a line whose carrier the
# runner reads or the corpus no longer has. Delete a line when its reader lands.
# The port has the readers (the text form and the message form are done); what
# is missing is the runner's dispatch, owed by docs/roadmap.sexp

column2: test/goose-hostile/runner.goose has no announce dispatch: the port's schema_rt::announce_read is never called on a corpus announcement, so the runner answers it absent
test/goose-hostile/runner.goose has no announce dispatch, and none that sets MsgVocabulary.max_bytes to the corpus's 8-byte bound: the runner answers it absent
test/goose-hostile/runner.goose has no announce dispatch, and none that sets MsgVocabulary.max_entries to the corpus's 1-entry bound: the runner answers it absent
test/goose-hostile/runner.goose has no announce dispatch, so a second schema_rt::announce_read on one vocabulary is never made: the runner answers it absent

conformance_message (conformance_unit.goose) always reads the unit's own announcement before the batch, so the runner cannot hand <Root>LoadMessages a vocabulary that was never announced: the runner answers it absent
test/goose-hostile/runner.goose has no text dispatch: the port's schema_rt::json_load_table is never called on a corpus text, so the runner answers it absent
